messages:
Maya (Support): Heads-up — scheduling a maintenance window for runtime nodes this Thursday 02:00–04:00 UTC. Need a short statuspage blurb + customer email template. Anyone taking the comms draft? :wave:
Liam (Eng): I can review. Are we doing a graceful drain + canary first or a full rolling restart?
Priya (Oncall): Plan is rolling restarts by AZ with canary on one small pool first. If canary fails -> rollback to previous pinned runtime.
deploy-bot: Maintenance ticket created: MAINT-2026. Dry-run scheduled Wed 08:00 UTC.
Maya (Support): Thanks. Drafting statuspage snippet now — keeping it concise. Posting draft below for quick review. Please reply with edits by EOD today.
Maya (Support): ```Status: Maintenance in progress
Impact: Brief request latency increases and ephemeral 5xx errors for a subset of inference requests in affected regions.
Window: Thu 02:00–04:00 UTC
What we're doing: Rolling runtime restarts with canary verification to apply kernel and driver upgrades. We will revert any canary that shows regressions.
Customer action: No action required. If you have pinned dedicated capacity or private deployment, we will not touch your nodes unless you opted into the upgrade. For questions, contact support@redwood.ai.```
Liam (Eng): Snippet looks good. Suggest adding line about SLA — "No expected SLA impact; we will notify if rollback affects committed latency SLO."
Maya (Support): Good call. Adding that.
Maya (Support): Email subject draft: "Planned maintenance: runtime networking and kernel updates — Thu 02:00 UTC"
Maya (Support): Email body (short): ```Hi —
We will perform a rolling maintenance window on our inference runtime on Thu 02:00–04:00 UTC. You may see short-lived increased latency or transient errors. We expect no sustained SLA impact; we'll notify if rollback or extended downtime is required.
If you have dedicated or private deployments and do NOT want this update applied, reply to this message before Wed 18:00 UTC and we'll exclude your environment.
Thanks,
Redwood Support```
Priya (Oncall): Add instruction for support to escalate: "If customer reports persistent errors after window, tag #oncall and include request ids."
Maya (Support): Added escalation line. Also adding simple checklist for post-maint verification in the ops runbook: run health-checks, sample requests to pinned models, verify latency percentiles (p50/p95), check error budget.
Liam (Eng): Reminder: pin previous runtime image as fallback and ensure canary autoscale set to 1-2 instances only. I'll create the rollback playbook and attach link here once ready.
Liam (Eng): attach: rollback-playbook.md (will post link in the ticket).
Maya (Support): One small ask — include a one-liner for the statuspage 'updates' stream so we can post progress messages: e.g. "02:00 — Canaries started; 02:20 — Canary pass; 02:30 — Rolling to remaining pools; 03:40 — Final pass complete."
Priya (Oncall): That timeline is fine. If canary fails, update sequence: "02:10 — Canary failed; 02:15 — Rollback initiated; 02:25 — Rollback complete; 02:35 — Monitoring".
Support Bot: Reminder: Customer notification cutoff Wed 18:00 UTC.
Maya (Support): Great — I'll post the statuspage update at the start of the window and send the email now (draft to send list). Tagging @Liam for the rollback doc link when available. :thumbsup:
Liam (Eng): Will drop the playbook link into MAINT-2026 before EOD.
Maya (Support): Thanks everyone. Final action items: 1) Maya send email + statuspage draft published, 2) Liam finalize rollback playbook, 3) Priya verify canary runbook & alerts, 4) Support watch channel during window.
Priya (Oncall): Oncall will watch and escalate as needed.
Maya (Support): Closing thread — will follow up with statuspage URL and email send receipt. :white_check_mark:
